newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Western bank said seeking Russia steel mill stake.
newsitem.headline: Western bank said seeking Russia steel mill stake.

text.p: An unnamed western bank is hoping to buy a minority stake in Russian steelmaker Novolipetsk Metals Combine (NLMK), the Russian International Metallurgists Union said on Tuesday.

U.S. law firm Meyer, Brown and Platt have sent a letter to the Russian government and to the heads of the chambers of parliament on behalf of a client, an unnamed western bank, offering to buy a 15 percent stake in NLMK held by Bank MFK for $96 million, a statement from the union said.
The statement said the law firm would also send a letter to Bank MFK, associated with Russia's powerful Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), making the same offer.
But a press spokesman for Bank MFK said on Tuesday he knew nothing of the offer and that the bank was not planning to sell the stake.
Government spokesman Igor Shabdurasulov and a spokesman for the State Property Committee, which was also said to have been sent a letter, said they had not heard of the deal either.
Bank MFK received the stake in return for a credit to the Russian government in 1995 under the controversial shares for loans scheme.

Bank MFK, along with fellow minority Novolipetsk steel mill shareholders Renaissance Capital and Cambridge Capital Management, won a court battle over investor rights with plant management last month.
